problem: The discovery dedup reference proves local filesystem create-if-absent semantics, but the canonical GitHub repository proposal-claim path has no host-specific atomic race canary.
acceptance: two or more concurrent attempts for one fingerprint yield exactly one durable repository pin
losers receive collision evidence and do not overwrite
source proposals and lineage remain preserved
no queue or authority promotion occurs
title: Canary GitHub proposal-pin races
mission: Exercise the canonical GitHub proposal-claim path with a bounded concurrent create-if-absent canary and persist winner/loser evidence proving exactly-one-winner, no-overwrite and lineage-preserving semantics without granting queue or promotion authority.

information_gain.reason: The current discovery evidence proves filesystem wx behavior but explicitly leaves repository-host create-if-absent semantics untested.

regression_prevention.reason: A real host race canary would detect any connector or repository behavior that permits duplicate proposal pins or winner overwrite despite the local reference implementation.

goal_relevance.reason: Surplus-capacity discovery depends on deterministic deduplication under many identical workers, so host-level atomicity is a direct prerequisite for trustworthy high-parallelism operation.

falsification: Two concurrent create-if-absent attempts for the same fingerprint both persist durable winner pins.
A losing attempt overwrites or mutates winner bytes.
Collision evidence cannot identify the pre-existing winning pin after the race.
The canary promotes its proposal into queue, Current, Human Accepted or Served authority.
dedup_note: The discovery-dedup implementation already validates local fs.open('wx') races. This proposal is deliberately limited to the unresolved repository-host primitive named by that return and does not duplicate the broader discovery implementation or 50-worker stress verifier.
